searches.question: Who appoints Australian heads of mission, and on what legal basis?
searches.route: web search "Australia heads of mission appointed by Governor-General commission ambassador 'Executive Council' DFAT appointment process high commissioner"; curl of https://www.dfat.gov.au/sites/default/files/dfat-foi-lex13382.pdf and https://foreignminister.gov.au/node/4509
searches.note: search snippets (DFAT FOI LEX 13382, Foreign Minister media releases) say heads of mission are appointed by the Governor-General acting on the advice of the Federal Executive Council, under the executive power in Chapter II of the Constitution, after the foreign and trade ministers decide with the Prime Minister's concurrence; agrement of the receiving State is sought under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. Both documents timed out (dfat.gov.au, no response in 120 s; foreignminister.gov.au 301 then timeout); neither is held. The statute that shows the practice is the Public Service Act 1999 s 39 (SRCH-15).

searches.question: Does any statute provide for the appointment of heads of mission?
searches.route: api.prod.legislation.gov.au titles search 'Public Service Act 1999', versions/find(titleId='C2004A00538',asAtSpecification='Latest'); PDF from www.legislation.gov.au; text searched for 'Head of Mission'
searches.note: Compilation No. 22 (C2024C00795). s 39: the appointment of a Head of Mission by the Governor-General cannot take effect unless the person is an APS employee; s 7 defines Head of Mission to include the head of a consular mission.
